messages:
maya: Quick thought 1: instead of forcing clients to do PII redaction, what if we send a compact tenant consent token + route-hint and perform deterministic redaction and sampling inside our pipeline?

sam: How is that materially different from today's per-route sampling + client-scrub?

maya: Two main diffs: (A) tenant consent is canonical (opt-in/opt-out + field-granularity mask) so scrub rules are stable; (B) sampling happens after redaction so our telemetry and billing don't get biased by dropped PII.

ben: Post-redaction sampling sounds right for analytics, but big concern: where does the raw payload live before scrub? we can't persist raw text.

maya: No writes to disk unredacted. Plan: ephemeral in-memory stage (TTL 5s) in the ingestion flow: decrypt consent -> scrub -> compute fingerprints/metrics -> drop raw text. All persistence is redacted or sealed.

priya: Operators sometimes need to inspect full requests for debugging. Can we emit a sealed debug blob to a separate RBAC'd store when tenant allows? should be gated by an inspect-lease that expires.

leo: +1 for sealed debug blob gated by per-tenant debug flag + short lease. Also require legal/ops approval flow in console.

sam: Console UX question: customers will want visibility into what was redacted. Suggest a "redaction diff" panel in request inspector that shows anonymized snippets and a list of scrub rules applied. Default to summary, expand for detail only for authorized roles.

ben: Telemetry: emit redaction_applied_count and redaction_false_negative_count per-route and per-tenant. We can alert if FN rises. Also emit sample_reason tag (e.g., post_redact, canary).

devops-bot: deploy-check: redaction_false_negative_count must be emitted at scrub stage and include sample_reason, route, tenant.
